archive_policy: 3.0, 3.1 and 3.2 arithmetic and evidence-extraction methods remain replayable. The new observation input is optional and omitted from older archives. Every primary result has an immutable source quotation and an explicit extraction version.
purpose: A single primary result can be investigated before a publication time series exists. This is a low-confidence observation hypothesis, not verified novelty or a forecast.
completed_year_history: Unchanged: 6 to 10 completed years, adjacent final three-year windows. Current-year results are separate evidence; they never increment completed-year studies or produce annual growth rates.
mature_categories: The complete 3.2 gates and formulas are retained for reviewed early signals, confirmed trends, emerging candidates, established topics and renewed interest. Sparse current-year primary evidence may remain a low-confidence observation after one annual dip, explicitly preserving the decline concern; persistent decline and large bursts do not gain an early label.
primary_observation_admission: Specific frozen technology with exact title membership and grounded query scope
At least one archived, dated primary research result, quoted from an abstract and supporting a case claim
First known observation is 0 to 3 years old, using any known earlier history and antecedents
Fewer than 10 distinct observed studies across the recent history and bounded primary evidence packet

No reviewed established, renamed or application-only novelty decision; no known complete-series older baseline or persistent decline. One annual dip is allowed only with a new current-year primary result and a visible concern
No withdrawn work, literature synthesis, dataset, supplementary asset, unsupported future experiment or explicit contrary conclusion
relaxed_requirements: For the new weak_signal_candidate observation lane only: one study suffices; the current year is allowed; complete history, an OpenAlex field denominator, publication growth, a novelty assertion, problem and advantage statements are not admission prerequisites. Unknowns stay unknown and are displayed as limitations. A grounded concrete primary case remains mandatory.
interpretation: Computational and theoretical primary results are research observations, never evidence of experimental demonstration or deployment. An author's implementation is not an independent replication. An observation without novelty evidence is not a verified novel mechanism.
signal_priority: Existing bibliometric signals retain their 3.2 priority. Newly admitted primary observations receive the same fixed watchlist priority of 10, with stable identifier ordering: no fabricated growth, volume bonus or calibrated probability. Stage still precedes numerical ordering.
quality: New observation hypotheses have partial data quality, low confidence and growth_confirmed=false even when a complete zero-history query was performed.
validation_status: Behaviour is checked on explicit synthetic positive and negative cases, source-unit regressions and legacy replay. These checks do not measure independent scientific precision, recall, commercial success or predictive lead time. Thresholds are documented operational choices pending independent labelled validation.
